resources.string: Device privacy
App lock, notification privacy and screen protection
These app protections work on supported Android devices, including GrapheneOS. Device-specific guidance is optional and does not enable system features.
App protection
Ask your keyboard to avoid learning from messages. This depends on the keyboard respecting the request.
Permissions and scopes
Contact access
Open app info, then Permissions → Contacts. On GrapheneOS, use Contact Scopes to share selected contacts. Other contacts stay hidden and editing device contacts is blocked.
Photo and file access
Open app info to manage photo and storage permissions. On GrapheneOS, Storage Scopes can limit shared files. You can also attach files using the system picker.
Network and exploit protection
Open app info to review device controls. On GrapheneOS, keep Network enabled for messages and calls. Leave exploit protection compatibility mode off unless needed to resolve a specific failure.
Notification privacy
Manage system notifications and lock-screen visibility. Use GhostWeb notification settings to choose whether names and message text appear.
Automatic system backup disabled

Android cloud backup and automatic device transfer are excluded, including account recovery tokens. This does not delete older backups. Signal and Molly backup or transfer features that you start yourself remain separate.
GrapheneOS privacy guide
Read about scopes and system protections on grapheneos.org
Optional device guides
Device password, fingerprint and auto reboot

Open Security settings. On GrapheneOS, configure a long device password, fingerprint unlock and auto reboot there. These protect the device and are separate from the Molly passphrase and app lock under Privacy.
User profiles and end session

Open system Settings, then System → Multiple users. On GrapheneOS, manage profiles, installation restrictions and available apps there. Ending a secondary profile session stops its apps, including message delivery until it starts again. Signal registration and contacts belong to each profile separately.
VPN leak protection

Open VPN settings. Where supported, enable Always-on VPN and Block connections without VPN for your trusted VPN app. A blocked or disconnected VPN can prevent Signal messages and calls. GhostWeb does not configure a VPN or verify leak protection.
Location access and indicator

Open app info to review Location permission. Grant access only when needed to share your location. On GrapheneOS, the system shows an indicator during location access; GhostWeb does not control that indicator.
Disable GhostWeb in system settings
Open app info. GrapheneOS supports disabling user-installed apps. Disabling GhostWeb stops messages, calls and background work until you enable it again.
GrapheneOS Camera and PDF Viewer
Read about these separate apps in the GrapheneOS feature guide. Install and select them through your device when appropriate. The existing GhostWeb camera and attachment handling stay available.
System logs and crash reports
Read about the GrapheneOS log viewer and crash reporting. Review logs before sharing. GhostWeb debug logs remain under Settings → Help; opening this guide does not upload a report.
Automatic OS updates

Read the GrapheneOS update guide. GrapheneOS installs OS updates in the background and supports automatic rollback if the first boot fails. Update settings and restart timing are managed by the OS. GhostWeb app updates are separate.
Unlock for sensitive quick settings
Read about GrapheneOS protections for sensitive system quick settings. The OS requires unlocking for protected actions. GhostWeb does not control system tiles or add a quick-settings tile.
App lock and automatic lockdown
Return to Privacy to configure the existing Molly passphrase lock, automatic lockdown and biometric app lock. These protect GhostWeb on supported Android devices without GrapheneOS.
